rationale: This is a deflator swap on the archive's existing leader (TotalCashUsesRequirement) rather than a new mechanism, and because ppent+invt approaches zero for asset-light firms the ranked ratio will largely sort on inverse tangibility/intangible intensity — a channel the archive has already probed — so any improvement would be hard to attribute to borrowing-base capacity.

A clean, internally consistent leg-substitution diagnostic with a real coverage payoff, but note that capx + Δinvt − ib scaled by assets is close to the union of the published investment/asset-growth, inventory-growth and profitability anomalies, so an FF5-adjusted survival would need careful interpretation rather than being read as new evidence.

Accumulated-depreciation-to-gross-plant is a genuinely new stock construct in this archive and the "deferred replacement obligation versus voluntary discipline" framing is economically coherent and sign-consistent, though the reused NEG(oancf/lt) leg has already produced −0.03 to −0.055 alphas on its own, so the incremental contribution of the vintage leg must be shown rather than assumed.

Conditioning the funding requirement on leverage relative to the firm's own five-year maximum is a substantively different fragility concept (capacity exhaustion, not indebtedness level) that plausibly avoids the structural-leverage loading that undermined earlier variants, with the caveat that the bounded ratio piles a large mass at exactly 1.0 and may coarsen the conditioner's ranks.

Extending the mechanism to the labor margin is a reasonable and sign-consistent test, but the first leg is the published hiring-rate anomaly in raw form and the second leg is the archive's most-reused conditioner, so the signal risks being a known anomaly times an already-validated distress leg rather than new evidence.

The level-versus-innovation decomposition of the archive's strongest construct is a defensible diagnostic and correctly signed, but it is a standard own-history demeaning of an existing signal (and the INTERACTION_TYPE label "novel" is inaccurate — it is a time-series deviation, not an interaction), and comparable change-based legs in this archive have already failed.
